claims.text: Retention of toughness in single-phase FCC high-entropy alloys is governed by stacking-fault energy.
At an SFE near 30 ± 5 mJ/m^2, perfect dislocations in CrMnFeCoNi dissociate into Shockley partials that can have large separation distances.
The separation distance between Shockley partials controls stacking-fault and deformation-twin formation.
Deformation twinning supplies strain hardening that inhibits necking and enhances ductility.
Excessively high SFE suppresses deformation twinning.
Excessively low SFE favors brittle FCC-to-BCC or FCC-to-HCP phase transitions.
Suppressed twinning or deformation-induced phase transitions reduce the ability to delay crack initiation and therefore lower toughness.
CrMnFeCoNi forms an FCC solid solution and has a stacking-fault energy near 30 ± 5 mJ/m^2.
High-temperature homogenization ensures minimal intergranular precipitation in the proposed baseline alloy.
Increasing Mn lowers SFE, whereas adding Al raises SFE, in the proposed CrMnFeCoNi-based alloys.
Alloying variations can systematically tune SFE while retaining a single-phase FCC structure.
Using an inert or vacuum environment from 77 K to 400–800°C avoids oxidation or corrosion as confounding effects.

Alloys with an intermediate SFE of about 30 ± 5 mJ/m^2 will have greater strain hardening, delayed necking, and greater toughness than otherwise comparable alloys with substantially higher or lower SFE.
CrMnFeCoNi has excellent damage tolerance, ductility of about 60–70%, and fracture toughness exceeding 200 MPa√m.
The proposed SFE-governed behavior applies to single-phase FCC HEAs dominated by dislocation-mediated plasticity.
The hypothesis may not apply to multiphase HEAs or alloys with substantial grain-boundary precipitation.
The hypothesis may not apply when diffusion-controlled high-temperature processes dominate deformation.
The relative contribution of twinning and other deformation mechanisms can vary with temperature and strain rate.
Stacking-fault energy can be estimated from the separation distance between coupled Shockley partial dislocations.
